context: Naoko has come to Kyushu for a wholesale ingredient buy. Goro is sitting on a bench by the fish market — the only other customer at the early-morning auction.
purpose: two old strangers, Kansai meets Kyushu — incidental bench-talk

lines.speaker: naoko_aunt
lines.style: Loud Kansai opener. Plops down two metres from him on the bench.

lines.speaker: goro_grandpa
lines.style: A slow Kyushu line. Doesn't look over.

lines.speaker: naoko_aunt
lines.jp: なるほどなあ。私、大阪。ラーメン屋。
lines.en: Ah, makes sense. I'm from Osaka. Ramen shop.
lines.style: Instant intel-sharing. Kansai economy — as the scene allows it.

lines.speaker: goro_grandpa
lines.jp: ふん。ラーメン、最近食うた覚えがない。
lines.en: Hm. Haven't eaten ramen in a while, come to think of it.
lines.style: A small philosophical observation. Eyes on the water.

lines.speaker: naoko_aunt
lines.jp: なんと！本当に？うちの店、来た方がええで。
lines.en: What?! Really? You ought to come to my shop.
lines.style: Mock-outraged Kansai. A real invitation behind the bit.

lines.speaker: goro_grandpa
lines.style: A small dry observation. Slight Kyushu humor audible.

lines.speaker: naoko_aunt
lines.jp: ほな、私が、ここでラーメン作ったろか。
lines.en: Then I'll make ramen for you right here.
lines.style: A wild Kansai joke offer — genuine and unforced throughout.

lines.speaker: goro_grandpa
lines.jp: (small laugh)…本当に来そうで、怖いな。
lines.en: (small laugh) …Sounds like you might actually do it. Scary.
lines.style: A real Kyushu laugh, rare. Voice slightly amused.

lines.speaker: naoko_aunt
lines.jp: やるで。本当に。お互い、まだ時間あるしな。
lines.en: I would. Really. We've still got time, both of us.
lines.style: A small unguarded honest line — with steady attentive presence.
